newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal's Deuba seeks parliamentary confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Nepal's Deuba seeks parliamentary confidence vote.

text.p: Nepali Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba on Thursday proposed a motion for a crucial vote of confidence in his feeble 17-month-old coalition government in the lower house of parliament.

"Though it was not required for me constitutionally to prove my majority, I am moving the motion for a confidence vote with a view that this would strengthen the democratic exercise," Deuba told the Himalayan kingdom's House of Representatives.
Voting on the motion of support for the fractious three-party centre-right coalition was scheduled to take place after 3 p.m. local (0815 GMT), parliament officials said.
Deuba slipped into a minority last December when a censure motion against him, sponsored by the communist opposition, fell short by two votes.
He was not constitutionally required to seek a confidence vote but had vowed to do so in the next session of parliament, which began on Monday.
The constitution requires 103 votes to pass the motion in the 205-member House of Representatives.
On paper, the ruling coalition controls 111 members, including the speaker who does not normally vote. The communist opposition and its supporters have 94 votes.

Proposing the motion, the prime minister listed the government's achievements, which included a river water-sharing treaty signed with India last February and a pact that allows most Nepali goods duty-free access to Indian markets.
He said foreign donors had pledged $1 billion worth of aid to Nepal since the Nepali Congress-led government was voted to power in September 1995, replacing a communist government.
Deuba's tenure has been marked by bitter divisions within the ruling coalition.
The communists moved a no-confidence motion last December, hoping to cash in on a rift within the Rastriya Prajatantra Party, a key partner in Deuba's coalition that has 19 seats in parliament.
Deuba's Nepali Congress party, which commands 87 seats in parliament, has also been sharply critical of his performance.
